moveDecisions.rationale: Candidate 1 better reflects the partly unstable scope of the move’s transition from a transcendent cause to its further personal and timeless attributes.
Candidate 2 better captures the stable scope and recoverable comparative claim connecting the three identified facts, resurrection, and evidence for God.

The move expressly presents the absence of any need for God as its central argument, supporting candidate 2’s motion-level importance and burden contact; its sweeping prospective claims also make candidate 2’s materially unstable scope finding preferable.

Candidate 2 more accurately records direct contact with both the claimed causal requirement and its application beyond the universe; its precision and calibration findings also better fit the categorical assertion that causality arises with the universe.

Candidate 2 states the contacted explanatory-warrant issue more exactly, while candidate 1 better captures the partly unstable scope created by moving from unobserved suspensions of law to all divine intervention.

Although it does not answer the moral-grounding claim, the suffering argument supplies issue-bearing contrary evidence about God, making candidate 2’s relevant-nonanswer structure and stable-scope precision finding preferable.

Candidate 2 more precisely identifies contact with morality’s proposed evolutionary source while preserving the unanswered objective-validity issue; its explicitness and calibration findings better match the asserted evolutionary account.

Candidate 2 correctly treats the move as a partial answer to an evidential argument because mere logical compatibility does not reframe or resolve the probabilistic challenge; candidate 2’s possibility-level calibration remains faithful to the stated claim.
Candidate 1 better captures the move’s direct challenge to both the proposed natural zero-energy explanation and the inference that such an explanation removes the need for a transcendent cause.

Candidate 1 accurately limits contact to whether the relevant cosmic sequence had a beginning; the move does not address zero net energy or independently defeat the transcendent-cause termination claim.
Candidate 1 best captures direct contact with both the reliability of the Gospel reports and whether those reports warrant resurrection as the best explanation of the claimed facts.

Candidate 2 correctly identifies direct contact with the distinction between evolutionary origins and objective validity, while candidate 1’s higher charity value better reflects the move’s fair, explicit engagement with the evolutionary alternative.

Candidate 1 properly classifies the move as partial because it addresses improbability and divine-intervention evidence but not the reliability objection to the Gospel reports; its implicit-qualification precision and explicit-uncertainty calibration findings best fit the evidence.

Candidate 1 more accurately frames the one contacted issue as whether the resurrection inference begins from faith, while the categorical dismissal of theistic explanations supports its certainty-level calibration finding.

Candidate 1 accurately records contact with the evidence-over-faith objection and the demand that evidence decide cosmic beginnings, while recognizing no answer to the separate simpler-natural-explanation claim; its limited plausibility force best matches the careful statement.
